stories.title: The Two Horns
body: Dhul-Qarnayn was a king whose name the Qur'an gives without a lineage and whose story it gives without an ending: a man Allah established in the earth and gave the means to everything. He could have stopped at the first city of gold. Instead he kept travelling.

He travelled west to where the sun sets in a murky spring and found a people who lived without a shield against injustice. Then he travelled east, past lands where one nation had no cover from the sun, and still he judged between people with a fairness the Qur'an records in one sentence: this is the mercy of my Lord.

Between two mountains he found a people who barely understood speech, and they told him of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, raiders who left corruption in their wake. Make for us a barrier, they begged. They even offered a tribute. He answered with the words of a servant: what my Lord has established for me is better. Help me with strength, and I will build between you a wall.

He built it from sheets of iron and molten copper, a wall so high the raiders could not climb it and so solid they could not breach it. Then he said the sentence that is the whole man in one breath: this is a mercy from my Lord; and when the promise of my Lord comes, He shall level it to the ground; and the promise of my Lord is ever true. Power was never his possession. It was a trust with a return date.
stories.lesson: Dhul-Qarnayn owned the means of everything and kept holding it with an open hand. Authority is safe in exactly one place: over a heart that credits Allah for it.

stories.title: The Father's Counsel
body: Luqman was not a prophet, but wisdom arrived at his door and Allah mentions it as a title: We gave Luqman wisdom. And what does a wise man do with wisdom in a book of scripture? He hands it to a child, and the words that survived are those of a father speaking to his son.

O my dear son, do not associate anything in worship with Allah; indeed, association is a terrible wrong. Son, be kind to your parents, walk with them in this world courteously, and refuse to let any loyalty swallow the gate of the garden on your way to them. Son, establish prayer, command what is right, forbid what is wrong, and bear with patience whatever comes to you. And notice how he describes the scale: the virtue of a grain of mustard seed, hidden in the rock or the sky or the earth, Allah brings it out.

Then the smallest commands, dressed in the same weight: do not turn your cheek away from people in pride, do not walk the earth strutting, for Allah does not love any arrogant boaster. Walk at a moderate pace, and lower your voice, for the most disagreeable of voices is the braying of donkeys.

That is the whole curriculum: a creed first, then ties, then prayer, then courage, then the way you hold your face and your voice in a queue. Wisdom in the Qur'an is rarely grand. It is mostly the smallest things done in the right order.
stories.lesson: Luqman taught nothing academic. He taught a son where to put his feet: on Oneness, and on a path that is neither bowed nor swaggering.

stories.title: The Chosen Woman
body: The wife of Imran dedicated what was in her womb to the service of the sanctuary, and when she delivered a girl she kept her promise anyway: she named her Maryam and placed her under the protection of her Lord from the whispers of everything driven away.

Maryam grew in the mihrab, and Zakariyya the prophet kept finding provision in her chamber. From where is this? she was asked. And her answer is the trust of a child with a Lord: from Allah; indeed, Allah provides whom He wills without accounting. The angels then brought her the announcement no woman would receive again: Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of all the worlds. O Maryam, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate, and bow down with those who bow.

Then, alone in the east, she received a visitor in the form of a perfect man, and a word from Allah landed in her, and her retreat became a cradle. The pangs drove her to the trunk of a palm, and she said the words of every mother at the end of her strength: oh, that I had died before this, and had been a thing forgotten. A voice from beneath her told her not to grieve, to shake the palm and eat what fell, to drink from the stream at her feet; not one detail missing, not one mercy arrived late.

She came home with the baby, and the city of tongues met her at the door. The Book records what they said and what they were answered. Her story ends in the same Book that defends her: veracity in one sentence of Chapter Maryam, final in Chapter Ale-Imran. The one who trusts her Lord completely discovers that she was never, even for a heartbeat, alone.
stories.lesson: Allah chose a girl in an alcove and made her the sign of a whole chapter. Purity, patience and trust outrank every accident of your birth.

stories.title: The House Next Door to Pharaoh
body: Asiya was the wife of the man the Qur'an calls Pharaoh, the tyrant whose name is the very shorthand for arrogance. Living inside his palaces, eating from his tables, hearing his divine claims daily, she was one of the few people in the world who could see him from a distance of one conversation instead of one continent.

She saw the baby in the river as a providence, not a problem, and raised a prophet in the house of his enemy. She believed in Allah quietly while the throne room filled with witnesses to a lie, for which faith she was punished by the hands of her husband and threatened to the end.

In the moment of her greatest pain she did not ask to be rescued from the palace or repaid for a life of luxury. She raised her hands and asked for real estate in the only country she could not reach: my Lord, build for me, near You, a house in the Garden, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and deliver me from the wrongdoing people.

Allah used her as the second example of a believer in all the Qur'an, a woman of a disbeliever's household who made her own faith the whole of her skyline. Her female body dies in the regime; her soul's address is finalized: near You, a house.
stories.lesson: The palace did not own Asiya; Asiya outgrew the palace and asked for the house next to the Most Merciful. Your address in the Hereafter does not have to match your postcode here.

stories.title: The Sleepers of the Cave
body: They were young men in a city whose every ceiling had been hung with idolatry, and they were the ones who decided that the fingerprint of Allah on the world could not be in objects made by human hands. They said it to a society that did not want to hear it, and the door of the city began to close behind them.

They fled to a cave outside the walls with their faith as luggage, and before sleep took them they made the prayer of the cornered: our Lord, grant us mercy from Your presence and guide us in our affair. Then Allah closed their ears in the cave, and their sunlight passed over them while they turned from side to side.

They slept, and across the city the calendar turned. When they woke, one of them slipped into town with silver coins to buy food, afraid of being recognised, and the people of the city held the coins of an age no one had used for three hundred and nine years. The Book tells the world what the sleepers were in truth: young men who believed in their Lord, whom We increased in guidance.

The lesson the Qur'an draws is not about the number of the sleepers: the argument about how many of them there were is the distraction the Book explicitly dismisses. The lesson is the sentence: from among the people of that city, it was the youths who chose the hard road, and the cave that the world abandoned, and Allah Himself as their keeper.
stories.lesson: When a city stops making room for faith, faith is still on the move. The cave that scares everyone is where the mercy finds the youths.

stories.title: The Boat, the Boy, and the Wall
body: Musa, the prophet who spoke to Allah, once stood and told his people that he knew of no man on earth more knowledgeable than he, and the answer came from above: there is, at the meeting of the two seas. He set out with a young helper, a fish, and a promise, until they found one of Allah's servants on whom Allah had bestowed mercy and knowledge.

Musa asked to follow him, and was warned before the journey started: you will not be able to bear with me. How can you have patience with what you do not understand? And so with the boat: a hole was drilled in it, and the wood of the days of a poor family began to drink the sea. Then the boy: a child was met on the road and quietly returned to his Lord. Then the wall: standing in a town that had shown them no hospitality, a wall about to fall was repaired for free.

Musa, upon him be peace, objected his way through all three lessons and then the explanations arrived: the boat was the livelihood of the poor, about to be boarded by a king who seized every sound vessel; the boy was going to hurt and wrong his two believing parents, and whether a different world could endure him is not the child's question to answer, and Allah knew him and the two of them better; the wall belonged to two orphaned boys and their inheritance was sleeping inside it, and their father had been righteous.

Then the servant of Allah gave the sentence that stands over every unknowable providence: this is the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. Some stories are not unfriendly to you when they look like losses. The road that looks like the wrong road may be the only one that assembles the protection, and Allah knows best.
stories.lesson: Musa, the greatest prophet of his age, sat as a student at a knowledge above knowledge. Trust in Allah has a container: it holds what your eyes cannot explain.

stories.title: The King Allah Chose
body: The children of Israel came to their prophet after Musa and demanded what a nation at war demands: set a king over us. The prophet hesitated and asked the question that stings: are you sure you will fight when the fighting is written? They promised. And then the choice came down, and it was not a man anyone would have picked.

Allah chose Talut. A man of neither royal blood nor public wealth, so objectionable to the calculators that they lined up their reasons: he has no abundance of wealth. The prophet answered with the only résumé that counts: Allah has chosen him over you, and has increased him in knowledge and stature, and Allah gives His kingdom to whom He pleases.

The sign of his reign arrived as a relic carried the way markings of a promised inheritance travel: the Ark with what the children of Musa and Harun had left, borne by angels, a proof for a people who insisted on proofs.

Then the army marched to the river: whoever drinks from it is not of me. The desert of a test thinned the ranks until the crossing took the whole courage out of everyone but a few, and of the few, the ones who stood, then saw the enemy's numbers, then ran. The victory came through the one whom no one had named a soldier, and Dawud, the small boy in the formation, won the world with a hurled stone. Allah's chosen are chosen for reasons no register can hold: knowledge and stature, and pride that the process is His.
stories.lesson: A king was chosen by the One who knew the names that would carry the hurt. The ropes of nations do not answer to the weighing of men: they answer to the mercy of the One who weighs hearts.

stories.title: The Queen Who Consulted
body: A hoopoe bird came back to Sulayman's court with news from a kingdom beyond the sand: I found a woman ruling over a people, and she has been given of all things, and she has a great throne. Her people, the bird reported, prostrate to the sun instead of Allah.

Sulayman, king of wind and jinn, sent a letter, and the letter was short and heavy: in the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful; be not haughty with me, but come to me in submission. In the palace of Sheba, the queen called her council: advice, O nobles, in my affair; I would never decide a matter without you. They offered her armies. She offered them time: kings, when they enter a city, ruin it.

She sent the famous gift, and the king of discernment sent it back: will you help me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you. She came in person, and the throne of her kingdom arrived ahead of her by powers she could not see. Finally she was led to a courtyard that was not a pool but a palace paved with glass, and there she was asked to enter, and all her careful deductions gathered into one act. She understood that what she had been shown was the truth, and she said the sentence the Book preserves: my Lord, I have wronged myself, and I submit with Sulayman to Allah, the Lord of the worlds.

Allah honoured her not for the eyeshadow but for the reasoning: a queen with power took advice from everyone, sent envoys before armies, and recognised the moment her religion and her history were the same thing to discard. Her name has been curled by tradition into the wind that follows every retelling: and of her the Book keeps the moment she chose.
stories.lesson: A crown is no reason to decide alone. The Queen of Sheba governed by consultation, acted on evidence, and bowed when the truth arrived: wisdom saved her kingdom the ruin wars bring.

stories.title: The Fire in the Ditch
body: There was a king in the lands before, and he had a sorcerer, and the sorcerer grew old, so the king was told to send him a boy to train. On the road the boy met a monk, and the monk's prayers began to answer the boy's days, one mercy at a time, until the boy could cure the blind and the leper by the permission of Allah.

The king's court grew suspicious of a healer they had not licensed, and the tests came: the boy was made to choose between a master who healed by Allah and a throne that healed nothing. The sorcerer could not cure the blind man he was supposed to cure; the boy could, and the price arrived: the king would kill the boy and the monk and the people.

The killing went on for a while because a certain kind of power thinks it is writing the ending; then the king gathered the people on a plain and had a ditch dug and filled with fire, and the believers were brought to the edge of it. The Book remembers the ditch and the fuel and the fire and the witness: destroyed were the people of the ditch, the fire fed with fuel of wood, when they sat around it.

The king was told the one thing his torture had made true: he could not kill the boy except in the name of the Lord of the boy. So he did the thing he was told, and the boy died, and the people died, and the fire went out of the ditch when there was nothing left for it to eat except the ash of a whole generation in Arabia: one woman standing at the edge with a baby in her arms, and the baby saying, be patient, mother, for you are upon the truth.

In the following centuries, the phrase that the Qur'an attaches to this chapter is a mystery even to the most certain hearts: the people of the ditch were killed inside a story, and the story is literally the answer to the question: why do the good among us die?
stories.lesson: The fire of the ditch could have been avoided by one sentence of unbelief; the people chose the fire. Faith is not a claim about what happens to you in this world; it is the address of your heart which this world cannot burn.
